audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Trundle all seven stages — win[0] through win[6] and phases[0] through phases[6] every one reading Trundle, at ratings of 8/10, 8/10, 7/10, 6/10, 8/10, 7/10, 6/10 — in a lane the packet scores 44.36% over 266 games. The entry's own late paragraph ends 'You lost this lane'.
audit.why: Three independent sources agree the chart is inverted. The packet has Trundle at 44.36%; MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.nasus reads the same 44.36; and the mirror audit at audits/top/nasus__trundle.json worked the other side and concluded Trundle should hold only stage 1. The content prose on this very page already says Nasus takes over from level 4 and is 'genuinely unplayable in a solo fight' late. Level 1 is genuinely Trundle's — Chomp is a flat 3.5s bite against a champion whose only level-1 tool is a 7.5s Siphoning Strike — and nothing after it is.
audit.corrected: Trundle holds Level 1 only. Nasus owns Level 2 onward, matching the 44.36% headline, the entry's own prose and the mirror audit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say Chomp 'steals his AD' about a dozen times and never once connect it to Siphoning Strike. Nasus's Q is named only as 'his Q' or 'Q stacks'.
audit.why: This is the whole reason the bite matters here. Siphoning Strike is an attack-damage ability, Chomp is the only thing in the matchup that removes attack damage, and at a flat 3.5s it is up more often than Nasus can spend the stack — so the debuff can sit on him almost permanently. That converts a vague 'AD steal' into a direct tax on the one number he spends the entire game growing, and it is the argument for biting even when the trade looks unprofitable.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps the Attack Damage that Siphoning Strike's damage is built on, and at a flat 3.5s you can hold that debuff on him nearly permanently.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Q Chomp, cd 3.5, saps Attack Damage)

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice appears three times as a way to 'cut off his retreat' or 'zone him off your carries', with no cooldown and no explanation of why it works on this opponent specifically.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain, and Nasus has no dash, blink or leap anywhere in his kit — Siphoning Strike is a melee attack modifier, Wither is a debuff, Spirit Fire is a ground zone, Fury of the Sands is a self-buff. So a pillar dropped between the two of them ends the chase outright; there is nothing he can spend to get past it. That makes Pillar the single most valuable cooldown Trundle owns in this lane, and at 21/19.5/18/16.5/15 it is also the one he can least afford to waste.
audit.corrected: Nasus carries no dash of any kind, so a Pillar of Ice between you ends the chase outright. It is 21s at rank 1 — spend it on the disengage, never on chip.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, impassable terrain, cd 21/19.5/18/16.5/15)

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is the tracked ability in every string and never carries a number or a range. Spirit Fire is absent from both layers. Neither ultimate has a cooldown.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11 at 700 range, which is both the window ('trade inside the 15 seconds') and the reason short trades are mandatory rather than preferred — he can open it from well outside Chomp's 300. Spirit Fire is a flat 12s at 650 that reduces the Armor of everyone standing on it, so it both zones Trundle off the wave and undoes his armour purchases, and the entry never mentions it exists. Fury of the Sands and Subjugate are both 120/100/80, an exact mirror.
audit.corrected: Wither 15s at rank 1 from 700 range. Spirit Fire a flat 12s at 650 that reduces the Armor of anyone standing on it. Both ultimates 120/100/80.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (W cd 15/14/13/12/11 range 700; E cd 12 range 650; R cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'Nasus with Fury of the Sands active gains a giant HP pool and lifesteal that eats into your drain advantage' and whys[4] repeats it — the implication being to avoid Subjugating him while his ultimate is running.
audit.why: It cuts the other way. Fury of the Sands grants him increased Health and bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, and Subjugate steals a PERCENTAGE of the target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance, doubled over four seconds. Every stat his ultimate adds is a stat yours takes a slice of. The correct sequencing is therefore to let him press R and steal afterwards, which is the exact opposite of what the entry implies — and it is the same shape of reasoning as the K'Sante entry, only inverted, because All Out sheds resists while Fury of the Sands adds them.
audit.corrected: Fury of the Sands adds Health, Armor and MR — and Subjugate takes a percentage of all three. Let him press R first, then steal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (R Fury of the Sands: increased Health, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance)

audit.whatIsWrong: early and spikes[0] both say Chomp 'slows his attack speed'. late credits the lifesteal to 'his R', and the content layer never names Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement — no attack-speed component. The attack-speed reduction in this lane belongs to Wither, pointed the other way. And the lifesteal is Soul Eater, his passive, which is running from minute one rather than only during his ultimate — so Grievous Wounds is an early purchase against the grind, not a late reaction to Fury of the Sands.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps Attack Damage; the attack-speed cut is Wither's, on you. Soul Eater gives him lifesteal from level 1, so Grievous Wounds is an early buy.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (P Soul Eater, bonus Life Steal; W Wither, slows Move and Attack Speed)

edits.before: At levels 1-2 you have a genuine window: Chomp (Q) steals his Attack Damage on contact and slows his attack speed, so open every trade with an immediate Q auto and retreat before his Wither (W) comes out. He starts W at level 2 and once it lands on you inside Frozen Domain, your speed advantage evaporates and what should be a winning trade turns into a losing one. The plan is short burst trades — Q in, two autos, Q again on the third auto, walk out. Never let him Wither you while you are committed. Keep him off Q stacks by contesting his farm at the cost of some poke; every stack you deny matters more than any early kill.
edits.after: At levels 1-2 you have a genuine window: Chomp saps the Attack Damage that Siphoning Strike's own damage is built on, and at a flat 3.5s you can keep that debuff on him almost permanently. Open every trade with Q plus an auto and leave before Wither comes out. He takes it at level 2, and from 700 range on a 15s cooldown it strips both the move speed and the attack speed Frozen Domain just bought you. The plan is short burst trades — Q in, two autos, Q again on the reset, walk out. Deny stacks by contesting his farm; every stack refused is worth more than an early kill.

edits.before: By levels 4-5 his Q damage is already noticeable and Wither's slow magnitude climbs to the point where Frozen Domain cannot fully compensate. You can still win individual trades if Wither is on cooldown — use Pillar of Ice (E) to cut off his retreat, walk onto your W zone, and chain Chops — but the moment he lands Wither the fight tilts to him. At 6, Subjugate does steal his armor and MR in a meaningful way since he will be building defensive stats, but Nasus with Fury of the Sands active gains a giant HP pool and lifesteal that eats into your drain advantage. Only take the level 6 all-in if he is low and his Wither is already burned — do not force it.
edits.after: By levels 4-5 Siphoning Strike is already noticeable and Wither's magnitude climbs past what Frozen Domain compensates for. You can still win a trade inside Wither's 15 seconds: Nasus carries no dash anywhere in his kit, so a Pillar dropped between you ends the chase outright — there is nothing he can spend to get past it. Watch Spirit Fire as well, a flat 12s at 650 that reduces the Armor of anyone standing on it. At 6 the ordering matters: Fury of the Sands grants him Health, Armor and MR, and Subjugate takes a percentage of all three, so let him press R first and steal afterwards. Both ultimates run 120/100/80.

edits.before: A stacked Nasus is genuinely unplayable in a solo fight: his Q hits you for a third of your HP, Wither locks you at near-zero attack and movement speed, and his R lifesteal sustains through anything Subjugate and your passive healing can produce. Your role shifts entirely to team fights where you Subjugate an enemy tank or bruiser in the back line, not Nasus himself. Keep Pillar of Ice for zoning him off your carries and accept that the 1v1 is over. You lost this lane; make your drain ultimate count on the right target in 5v5.
edits.after: A stacked Nasus is unplayable in a solo fight: Siphoning Strike takes a third of your bar, Wither holds you at near-zero attack and movement speed, and Soul Eater's lifesteal runs from level 1, so Grievous Wounds belongs on your first back rather than your last. Your role shifts to team fights, where you Subjugate a different frontliner and keep Pillar of Ice for walling Nasus off your carries — he has no dash, so that wall holds. The 1v1 is over; make the drain count on the right target.
